title: On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents: Variance, Task Order, and Underspecification
abstract: arXiv:2608.18066v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Memory-based self-improving agents--those that learn from an online stream of tasks and improve over time by maintaining a textual memory bank--have shown great promise in recent literature. However, the reliability aspects of these methods have been critically overlooked. In this work, we conduct a comprehensive re-evaluation of two memory-based methods, broadening the scope of evaluation along two axes: (1) including multiple runs to quantify variance, and (2) randomly shuffling the tasks to investigate the effect of task order. Through these experiments, we make two observations that expose the fragility of current methods: First, agent evaluation is inherently noisy in complex environments and on multi-step tasks, and stacking a self-improving loop on top can further amplify this noise. translated_title: 关于自我改进智能体的脆弱性：方差、任务顺序与规范不足
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.18066v1 公告类型：新论文 摘要：基于记忆的自我改进智能体——即从在线任务流中学习，并通过维护文本记忆库随时间提升性能的智能体——在近期文献中展现出巨大潜力。然而，这些方法的可靠性方面被严重忽视。在本工作中，我们对两种基于记忆的方法进行了全面重新评估，沿两个维度拓宽了评估范围：（1）包含多次运行以量化方差，（2）随机打乱任务顺序以研究任务顺序的影响。通过这些实验，我们得出两个观察结果，揭示了当前方法的脆弱性：首先，在复杂环境和多步骤任务中，智能体评估本质上具有噪声性，而叠加自我改进循环可能进一步放大这种噪声。其次，智能体的改进高度依赖于任务顺序。先前工作常采用默认排序，这隐含地施加了一种课程学习，从而激活了...
tldr: 本文通过多运行方差分析和任务顺序随机化实验，揭示了基于记忆的自我改进智能体在评估噪声和任务顺序依赖上的脆弱性，指出其改进效果高度不稳定且受隐含课程影响。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals the fragility of memory-based self-improving agents through variance and task-order randomization experiments, showing their evaluation is noisy and improvement highly depends on task order.
